roadmap_title: Full Stack Acceleration Curriculum: Zero-to-Staff Readiness
executive_strategy: Targeted focus on concurrency, caching resilience, and database isolation to elevate your candidate profile to Senior tier.

stage_1_concept.title: Cache Stampede Invalidation & Probabilistic Expiration
key_takeaways: Cache stampede occurs when high-concurrency requests hit an expired key simultaneously.
XFetch algorithm or mutex locks (SETNX with TTL) prevent backend database collapse.
Dual-write consistency vs CDC (Change Data Capture) outbox pattern.
stage_1_concept.mental_model: Treat cache as an ephemeral acceleration layer; never rely on it as source of truth. Always isolate expiry from synchronous database recomputation.
stage_1_concept.recommended_reading: Redis Documentation on Distributed Locks (Redlock) and High Availability Sentinel/Cluster

stage_2_hands_on_task.title: Implement Atomic Redis Token-Bucket Rate Limiter with Lua
stage_2_hands_on_task.scenario: Design an Express middleware that protects a tier-1 payment endpoint from burst traffic without allowing race conditions between concurrent requests.
requirements: Use Redis EVAL with an atomic Lua script to decrement token counts and reset window.
Return standard HTTP headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After.
Handle Redis connection timeouts gracefully with fail-open or local in-memory fallback.

stage_3_retest_trigger.prompt: Suppose 10,000 requests hit your Redis token bucket rate limiter in the exact same millisecond. Describe how your Lua script guarantees zero race conditions compared to a standard Redis GET followed by INCR. Furthermore, if Redis goes offline, how does your middleware avoid taking down all traffic?
evaluation_criteria: Explains single-threaded atomic execution of Redis Lua scripts.
Points out that GET followed by INCR creates a check-then-act race window.
Describes graceful circuit-breaking / fail-open strategy during Redis downtime.

stage_1_concept.title: PostgreSQL Lock Contention, Index Scans & Connection Pooling
key_takeaways: Index scans (B-Tree, GiST, GIN) vs Sequential Table Scans.
Row-level locking semantics: SELECT FOR UPDATE vs SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
PgBouncer transaction-mode vs session-mode pooling and prepared statements.
stage_1_concept.mental_model: Every transaction holds locks until COMMIT or ROLLBACK. Minimizing transaction hold time is paramount for high throughput.
stage_1_concept.recommended_reading: PostgreSQL Official Manual: Chapter on Concurrency Control and Explicit Locking

stage_2_hands_on_task.title: Architect a Zero-Deadlock Background Job Queue with SKIP LOCKED
stage_2_hands_on_task.scenario: Build a persistent job dispatcher in Node.js where 20 background workers pull unassigned jobs from a PostgreSQL jobs table concurrently.
requirements: Write SQL transaction using SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED to prevent lock contention.
Ensure workers never process duplicate jobs or block each other.
Track retry counts and backoff failures into a dead-letter state.

stage_3_retest_trigger.prompt: Why does 'FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED' eliminate worker lock contention compared to standard 'FOR UPDATE' in high-volume queues? How does this interact with transaction isolation levels (Read Committed vs Repeatable Read)?
evaluation_criteria: Clarifies that SKIP LOCKED skips already-locked rows without blocking.
Explains that standard FOR UPDATE queues workers in lock wait queues.
Mentions serialization anomaly handling under Repeatable Read.

stage_1_concept.title: Zero-Downtime Deployments & Automated Canary Analysis
key_takeaways: Rolling updates vs Blue/Green vs Canary deployments.
Liveness, Readiness, and Startup probes in Kubernetes.
Automated rollbacks based on p99 latency and 5xx error rate thresholds.
stage_1_concept.mental_model: Deployments should be continuous, verifiable experiments. Never switch 100% traffic without validating real production telemetry first.
stage_1_concept.recommended_reading: Kubernetes Documentation on Pod Lifecycle and Deployment Strategies

stage_2_hands_on_task.title: Configure Canary Deployment with Automatic Rollback Metrics
stage_2_hands_on_task.scenario: Create a deployment specification routing 10% of live traffic to canary pods, rolling back automatically if HTTP 5xx responses spike above 1%.
requirements: Define readiness probes with appropriate initialDelaySeconds and failureThreshold.
Configure traffic splitting at ingress/service level.
Implement graceful SIGTERM shutdown handler in Node.js server.

stage_3_retest_trigger.prompt: What is the difference between a Kubernetes liveness probe and a readiness probe during a rolling deployment? What catastrophic cascade occurs if a slow database query causes a liveness probe to fail?
evaluation_criteria: Explains that readiness probe removes pod from service routing, while liveness restarts the container.
Explains that failing liveness restarts pods, exacerbating database load and causing death spirals.
